clue.text: Wretched strikes I had backed

indicators.note: something backed has been driven in reverse, so the letters run from right to left

blocks.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a miserable stretch of industrial action they once supported.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and wretched are synonyms for gloomy, miserable or of poor quality.

clue.text: Attach less importance to drink and fun

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it quickly
play is amusement or fun

explanation.surface: Someone makes light of a night of drinking and partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To downplay something is to make it seem less significant than it is.

clue.text: Doing wrong part of test, putting final piece first

indicators.note: the instruction tells you to take the last letter and move it to the front of the word

blocks.note: an innings is a team's turn to bat in a Test match in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer cheats during a session of an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, played over innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinning is committing sins, which is to say doing wrong.

clue.text: Person not drinking possibly eats in bar

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be put another way

blocks.note: the three words as written

explanation.surface: A teetotaller might still go to the pub just for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from something, especially alcohol, so is a non-drinker.

clue.text: What's absurd about clubs having boxer, perhaps, as guard?

indicators.note: an absurd arrangement is a nonsensical one, so the letters of the preceding word get jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the next item

blocks.note: the word rearranged
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
a boxer is a breed of dog, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a nightclub hiring a prizefighter as its bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer here is not a fighter but the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a dog kept to guard property, and by extension any body that guards against wrongdoing.

clue.text: Person taking responsibility for their life who doesn't believe in ghosts?

definitions.text: Person taking responsibility for their life who doesn't believe in ghosts?

blocks.clueFragment: Person taking responsibility for their life who doesn't believe in ghosts?
blocks.note: surface reading: a self-reliant sceptic who denies the supernatural

blocks.clueFragment: Person taking responsibility for their life who doesn't believe in ghosts?
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone writing their own life story without using a ghostwriter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Their life' is a written life story, and 'ghosts' are ghostwriters, not spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: This writer composes their own life story personally rather than hiring a ghostwriter to do it.

clue.text: Something grasped by athletic Aberdonian?

indicators.note: grasped by means held inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A strongman from Aberdeen hoists something at a Highland games.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a Scottish athlete grips the log before tossing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the long pole thrown in the Scottish Highland games event of tossing the caber.

clue.text: Remove human expertise from workplace in poor shape

blocks.note: a desk is where an office worker works
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Automation strips skill from an office that is already struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: To deskill a job is to reduce the expertise needed, often by machines doing the skilled part.

clue.text: Key admission for those in certain class

blocks.note: G is a musical key
entry is admission

explanation.surface: A key grants entrance to an exclusive social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key, but it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are people of good social position, the class just below the nobility.

clue.text: High-ranking strategist with mostly moral attitude, having multiple job applications

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer who plans campaigns
pure means morally clean
a pose is a posture or attitude

explanation.surface: A senior officer of mostly upright views is applying for many posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A general-purpose tool or item is suitable for many uses, rather than one specific job.

clue.text: Affected by moving air, part of orchestra's shed tears

blocks.note: the wind is a section of an orchestra, with its possessive
wept means shed tears

explanation.surface: A section of the orchestra is moved to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept describes a place or person exposed to and ruffled by strong wind.

clue.text: Petty officer on sub at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the two words as written

explanation.surface: A naval rating serves aboard a submarine on patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun (boatswain) is a ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew, a petty officer rank in navies.

clue.text: Server in force that's not controlled by state

blocks.note: first meaning: a soldier of the lowest rank, serving in the armed forces
second meaning: independent of government

explanation.surface: Someone serves in a police or military force that is independent of government.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the lowest army rank and anything run outside public ownership.

clue.text: Scottish author runs into obstacle

blocks.note: J. M. Barrie, Scottish author of Peter Pan
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Scottish writer jogs headlong into something blocking the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' reads like an insertion, but here it just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier is a fence or other structure that blocks passage, so it is an obstacle.

clue.text: Old vessel laid by nitrogen or another gas

blocks.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An ancient ship is laid up beside a tank of nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid by' simply places one piece next to the other; 'another' works because nitrogen is itself a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, the third most plentiful in Earth's atmosphere after nitrogen and oxygen.

clue.text: Very nice answer within one's competence put right in

indicators.note: the phrase literally says to place an item inside, so one letter is slotted into the middle

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
something doable lies within your capability
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for an answer that was easy enough and then corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful or charming, an informal way of calling something very nice.

clue.text: Second crop ruined at the farm

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the three words as written

explanation.surface: A late harvest has been spoiled on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: In its original farming sense, an aftermath is the fresh growth of grass mown after the first cut.

clue.text: Tough sergeant, say, time after time breaking soldier

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the letter is pushed inside the word for soldier

blocks.note: a marine is a soldier serving with a navy
T is the abbreviation for time
T again

explanation.surface: A harsh drill sergeant keeps cracking a recruit, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: One T goes inside the soldier and the second is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, the stereotypical harsh drill sergeant being an example.

clue.text: Unsuitable monarch succeeding one with mass support

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the physics symbol for mass
a prop holds something up
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A king takes the throne after a rival who had the backing of the masses, which is thought inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' tells you the monarch comes after the rest, even though it is read first.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means not fitting the rules or occasion, so it is a synonym for unsuitable.

clue.text: Awfully evil character, in common stereotype

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the next words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A wicked villain is a familiar cliche in fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' belongs with the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster is a cruel or wicked person, a dreadfully evil figure.

clue.text: Returning thus in performance in title role

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first word sits within the second
returning means going back the way you came, so the whole result is read backwards

blocks.note: an act is a performance on stage
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A star comes back to take on the leading part in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end: Tosca is the heroine and title part of Puccini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the singer Floria Tosca, whose name gives Puccini's opera its title.

clue.text: Particular places I recollected

indicators.note: read as re-collected, gathered up again, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: the two words as written

explanation.surface: Someone remembered certain spots they had visited.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular both mean specific, belonging to one case rather than in general.

clue.text: Rising in revolt over conflict diamonds

blocks.note: a populace that is up is in rebellion
war is armed conflict
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An uprising breaks out over blood diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first pieces above the last; it simply joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward describes movement towards a higher place, which is what rising means.

clue.text: Cat and part of flower shown on page

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
the anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a stamen

explanation.surface: A book page illustrates a cat beside a botanical diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown on' puts the page first, before the flower part.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, usually a black leopard or jaguar.

clue.text: Composer whose pieces could come in handy

indicators.note: the pieces are the letters of the name, which could be rearranged to fit the following word

blocks.note: the word as written

explanation.surface: A composer's musical works might prove useful.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer's letters, rearranged, spell the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian classical composer, often called the father of the symphony.

clue.text: Warning football team after one's sent off in Liverpool, for example

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the team goes within the city example

blocks.note: Liverpool is a major seaport

blocks.clueFragment: football team after one's sent off
blocks.note: a football side has eleven players, so with one sent off ten remain

explanation.surface: A Liverpool side, down a man after a red card, gets a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: The team number is not a word but a count: eleven less the dismissed player.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign or omen of something coming, usually bad, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: A permit legally voided — in a way that's how it should be

definitions.text: in a way that's how it should be

indicators.note: something voided has been emptied, leaving only the outside shell of each word

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its inside removed
the word with its inside removed

explanation.surface: A licence is legally annulled, which was only right.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means suitably or appropriately, in a manner that fits the case.

clue.text: Choice about time for work in theatre

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An actor weighs up when to take a stage job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, where surgeons work, not a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical operation is the work done in a hospital's operating theatre.

clue.text: Crazy leader of dissidents exploded grenade

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
something exploded is blown apart, so its letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the first letter
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad rebel chief has set off a hand grenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means mentally unbalanced, an established synonym for insane.

clue.text: At the same time that learner enters game

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the letter goes into the next word

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a British car
whist is a card game

explanation.surface: A novice joins a card game just as it is starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is the British variant of while, a conjunction meaning during the time that.
